claim.claim-text: 1. A head mounted display system (60) configured to project light to an eye (210) of a user (90) to display augmented reality image content in a vision field of the user (90), the head mounted display system (60) comprising:
2. The head mounted display system (60) of Claim 1, comprising a plurality of infrared light sources (934, 960) in which the first light source (934, 960) is included.

3. The head mounted display system (60) of Claim 2, wherein processing electronics (140) are configured to cause the plurality of infrared light sources (934, 960) to alternately pulse at different wavelengths.
4. The head mounted display system (60) of Claim 2, further comprising an in-coupling optical element (944) configured to couple light from the image projector (930) into the waveguide (940).

5. The head mounted display system (60) of Claim 4, wherein the in-coupling optical element (944) is in direct optical communication with the plurality of infrared light sources (934) and the image projector (930) such that light emitted by the plurality of infrared light sources (934, 960) is incident on the in-coupling optical element (944) prior to optically interacting with the coupling optical element (944) or the out-coupling element (952).

6. The head mounted display system (60) of Claim 5, wherein the waveguide (940) is configured to receive the light from the in-coupling optical element (944) and propagate the light through the waveguide (940) by total internal reflection along the coupling optical element (944) to maintain at least 90% of the light at each reflection.
7. The head mounted display system (60) of Claim 2, wherein the camera (920) is configured to:

capture a first region of a retina of the user's eye (210) when directed at a first angle relative to the waveguide (940); and capture a second region of the retina of the user's eye (210) when directed at a second angle relative to the waveguide (940).

8. The head mounted display system (60) of Claim 7, wherein the processing electronics (140) are configured to form a composite image of the retina of the user's eye (210) with the first and second regions.
9. The head mounted display system (60) of Claim 2, wherein the optical coupling optical element (944) comprises:
10. The head mounted display system (60) of Claim 1, wherein the image projector (930) is configured to:
11. The head mounted display system (60) of Claim 1, wherein the coupling optical element (944) is configured such that:

light from the environment in front of the user (90) wearing the head mounted display system (60) is coupled into the waveguide (940) and guided therein such that images of the environment may be captured by the camera (920); and light reflected from the eye (210) of the user (90) wearing the head mounted display system (60) is coupled into the waveguide (940) and guided therein such that images of the eye (210) may be captured by the camera (920).

12. The head mounted display system (60) of Claim 1, further comprising an eyepiece (950) disposed on the frame (80), the eyepiece (950) configured to direct light into the user's eye (210) to display augmented reality image content to the user's vision field; and wherein at least a portion of the eyepiece (950) is transparent and disposed at a location in front of the user's eye (210) when the user (90) wears the head-mounted display such that the transparent portion transmits light from an environment in front of the user (90) to the user's eye (210) to provide a view of the environment in front of the user (90).

13. The head mounted display system (60) of Claim 12, wherein the image projector (930) is configured to direct light into an edge of the eyepiece (950), which directs the light into the user's eye (210) to display augmented reality image content to the user's vision field.

14. A method carried out by a head mounted display system including a frame (80) configured to be supported on a head of a user (90), an image projector (930), a camera (920) coupled to the frame (80), a waveguide (940) coupled to the frame (80) and optically coupled to the camera (920), an optical coupling optical element (944) coupled to the frame (80), an out-coupling element (952) configured to direct light emitted from the waveguide (940) to the camera (920), and a first light source (934, 960) configured to direct light to the user's eye (210) through the waveguide (940), the method comprising:

15. The method of Claim 14, wherein the headset comprises a plurality of infrared light sources (934, 960) in which the first light source (934, 960) is included; and wherein the method further comprises controlling the plurality of infrared light sources (934, 960) to alternately pulse at different wavelengths.
